Relevance.description: How well content addresses its stated topic.

Bias.description: Systematic skew reflecting training data biases.

Coherence.description: Logical flow and consistency of argument.

Fluency.description: Surface readability. Slop is paradoxically fluent.
Fluency.note: High fluency + low density = strong slop signal

SuperficialCompetence.description: Grammatically correct, photorealistic or structured, but without depth, originality or genuine intention.

AsymmetricEffort.description: Minimal input (prompt) for mass output; lack of human revision, research or creativity.

MassProducibility.description: Scalable for algorithms (SEO, Feeds), often with clickbait elements.

signals.source: Consolidated from Shaib et al. 2025, empirical observation, community detection (Reddit r/LocalLLaMA, HN), slopdetector.org, glukhov.org, Willison 2024
signals.note: Signal words are PROBABILISTIC indicators, not proof. Human writers use some of these too. Threshold-based scoring required.

buzzwords.description: Words disproportionately used by LLMs vs humans. Tier = signal strength.

tier1_critical.description: Strongest AI markers. Almost never in casual human writing.

tier2_high.description: Very common in AI output, uncommon in human writing.
words: at the end of the day
in the grand scheme of things

tier3_moderate.description: Common in both AI and corporate/buzzword-heavy human writing.

phrases.description: Multi-word patterns characteristic of AI generation.

items: at the end of the day
when all is said and done
as the digital landscape continues to evolve
the world of [X] is undergoing a profound transformation
in recent years, [X] has emerged as
whether you're a seasoned [X] or just starting out
as we look to the future,
at the end of the day

indicators.note: Em-dashes are rare in casual human writing but extremely common in GPT/Claude output

indicators.pattern: Conclusion restates introduction with synonym substitution
Every section same length regardless of topic importance
Zero grammar errors + identical formality throughout
indicators.note: Weak signal alone — professional editors also produce this

punctuation.description: Punctuation anomalies characteristic of AI output.

indicators.description: Faces with subtle but detectable wrongness
Letters that don't form real words
Bizarre AI imagery mixing unrelated concepts
Comment on every line including obvious ones
Extremely long descriptive variable names everywhere
Methods that don't exist in the library

german.note: German AI output often mixes Denglisch (English loanwords) with formal register

buzzwords: dans un monde en constante évolution

canonicalDefinition.definition: Digital content created with generative AI and perceived as low-effort, low-quality, generic, superficial or lacking in meaning. Mass-produced for the attention economy, clicks, advertising revenue or other monetary benefits.

necessaryConditions.condition: Generative AI is the primary source of the content
Human care, curation or verification is lacking
The content is published/distributed unsolicited (push rather than pull)

canonicalDefinition.exclusion: Carefully curated, reviewed and intentionally published AI-assisted outputs are explicitly excluded from this definition (Willison 2024; Shaib et al. 2025 §3).

coreParadigm.statement: AI slop is not a binary media type but a risk profile.
coreParadigm.implication: Content can be AI-generated and high quality. Conversely, human spam can be worthless. Slopness arises from the combination of generation, care, scaling, distribution, provenance and quality.

scoringFormula.formula: slop_score = min(1.0, sum(weights[s.severity] * s.confidence) / max(1, n))

thresholds.block: hardcoded secrets OR SQL injection OR child safety violation

limitations: Subjectivity of binary slop judgments: Cohen's κ -0.15 to 0.29 (Shaib et al. 2025) → dimensional scoring more robust
Reflexivity: detection heuristics become known → producers adapt ("humanized" variants)
False positives on human text: templated journalism, boilerplate
Context dependence: technical documentation may use repetition for clarity
Linguistic bias: detection strongest in English; weaker in Hindi, Vietnamese, Urdu — exactly where a lot of slop is produced
Evolving models: new model generations produce new slop patterns; ontology needs regular updates
Philosophical critique (Puliafito): "Slop" describes mediocrity — but mediocrity is the baseline of all cultural production
